question.worked_solution:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{4},$ we will set our result equal to $\frac{1}{4}.$ 

From the equation $y=(2x+k)(x-3k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=-\frac{k}{2}$ and ${x}_{2}=3k.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{k}{2}+3k)}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{6k-k}{2})}{2} \\  & =\frac{5k}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{4}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5k}{4} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ 5k & =1 \\ k & =\frac{1}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
